change.title: pr-2
change.description: FEATURE: per-topic unsubscribe option in emails
change.author: Régis Hanol

findings.title: unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser row
findings.body: `TopicUser.find_by` returns nil when the user never visited or tracked the topic. The next line then calls `tu.notification_level` and raises NoMethodError, so the user gets a 500. This happens for a user who was emailed about a topic through a mention or a watched category without ever opening it. If `notification_level` is nil, the comparison also raises. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic_id, notification_level: ...)`, which creates the row, publishes the MessageBus update and handles nil levels. Treat a nil level as regular.

findings.title: State change on a GET with no confirmation
findings.body: A plain GET changes the notification level and saves it. Email clients, link scanners and prefetchers fetch links in emails, so they can unsubscribe or mute the user without the user clicking. The GET also skips the CSRF protection that a POST would have. Make the change on an explicit user action, for example a button on the page that sends a PUT to `set_notifications`.

findings.title: Unsubscribe link needs a logged-in session, but the email is not tied to one
findings.body: `ensure_logged_in` is applied, so a user who is not logged in is sent to login. This is only a concern if the login redirect does not bring them back to the unsubscribe URL. The topic is also loaded with `TopicView.new` before the slug redirect, and I did not check whether the redirect branch needs the full view. The JSON branch relies on `perform_show_response`, which the diff changes to add `render :show`. I did not check that this does not alter the `show` action.

findings.title: Typo in property name: stopNotificiationsText
findings.body: The name is misspelled ("Notificiations"). The same misspelling is used in the template at `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs:3`. Rename it in both files.

findings.title: Topic title rendered unescaped with triple-stash
findings.body: The template uses `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}`, and `fancyTitle` is already HTML. I assumed it is sanitized on the server. If any path puts raw user text into it, this becomes an XSS hole. Also, the dropdown-button change inserts `title` into the buffer without escaping, but that was already the case before this PR.

contracts.before_after: The existing path goes through TopicUser.change, which creates the row and publishes the change. The new path edits the row directly with save! and assumes the row exists.
contracts.visible_effect: The page renders the topic show template, and the client unsubscribe route displays the notification button.
contracts.failure_mode: A missing TopicUser row causes a NoMethodError and a 500.

summary: The new unsubscribe action crashes with a 500 when the user has no TopicUser row. It also changes the notification level on a GET, so email link prefetchers can trigger it. The rest is formatting churn and a typo in a property name. I read `topics_controller.rb` up to line 130 and `topic.rb` lines 700–725. I did not open the other changed files in full, and I confirmed nothing outside the controller and the topic URL.
